In commit 9a69e2b385f4 (""bpf: Make remote_port field in struct
bpf_sk_lookup 16-bit wide"") the remote_port field has been split up and
re-declared from u32 to be16.
However
column2: the accompanying changes to the context access converter have not

column1: been well thought through when it comes big-endian platforms.
Today 2-byte wide loads from offsetof(struct bpf_sk_lookup
are handled as narrow loads from a 4-byte wide field.
This by itself is not enough to create a problem
1. 32-bit wide access to ->remote_port backed by a 16-wide wide load
2. inherent difference between litte- and big-endian in how narrow loads
need have to be handled (see bpf_ctx_narrow_access_offset)
we get inconsistent results for a 2-byte loads from &ctx->remote_port on LE
and BE architectures. This in turn makes BPF C code for the common case of
2-byte load from ctx->remote_port not portable.
To rectify it
column2: inform the context access converter that remote_port is

column1: 2-byte wide field
column2: and only 1-byte loads need to be treated as narrow

column1: loads.
At the same time
column2: we special-case the 4-byte load from &ctx->remote_port to

column1: continue handling it the same way as do today
existing BPF programs working.
